name: vision-agent
title: A Vision Agent
claim: One agent answers a question about the files it is given, in plain words, by writing code that looks, listens and judges, and ends with a report that cites every claim at the file's own page, second or region.

oneOf.why: The lead and the eyes (google/gemini-3.8-flash, which take a video window with its sound).
The lead and the eyes (openai/gpt-6-luna and openai/gpt-6-sol, which take frames, not video) when it is the only key.
The lead and the eyes (anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5, which takes frames) when it is the only key.
An OpenAI-compatible gateway that serves the models under their public ids, instead of provider keys.
oneOf.where: your gateway's base URL, ending in /v1

keys.why: A model provider's key for --live (the run names every model by provider and public id).

oneOf.why: Jev at TypeSafe: jev-1.14.0, the first Jev that draws boxes, judges frames and pages.
Jev through OpenRouter, when it serves jev-1.14.0 (boxes need that model).

keys.why: A Jev key: the judge that scores frames and pages and draws boxes.
Scribe v2 on fal, which writes what a recording says with each word's second; not needed when the gateway passes fal's queue through (/fal-queue).

programs.why: The agent's code cuts frames, windows, clips and audio with it.
The agent's code reads a recording's length with it.
The agent's code renders PDF pages with it (poppler).
The agent's code reads a PDF's text layer with it, when the PDF has one (poppler).
The transcribe skill names a recording's folder with it.

input.shape: examples/vision-agent/agent.ts, Input: the question in plain words, and the names of the files in the workspace
input.default: an example folder's question.md and inputs.json (npm run demo:vision -- examples/<folder>)
